content:
Henry Cho: Quick approval request for user-facing terminology + messaging for the examples refresh (streaming + tools + structured output). We’re trying to lock this today so Docs + SDK READMEs can land cleanly.

Henry Cho: Proposed decisions:
1) Use “tool calling” everywhere (not “function calling”), but add one short note “tool calling (aka function calling)” for migration/search.
2) Use “structured output” as the primary term; mention “JSON schema” explicitly; avoid “JSON mode” except maybe in a FAQ line for folks coming from older snippets.
3) Streaming docs: describe “stream events” and keep event names consistent with the gateway: `response.output_text.delta`, `response.tool_call.delta`, `response.completed`.

Henry Cho: Also need sign-off on changelog language + launch announcement blurb (PLG audience). Draft is here: https://docs.redwood.example/changelog (staging) — would love thumbs up / edits.

Nikhil Sharma: +1 on “tool calling” as primary. “Function calling” is overloaded in competitor docs; “tool calling” is clearer.

Nikhil Sharma: For migration/search, I like a single parenthetical the first time it appears and maybe one entry in the glossary/FAQ.

Elliot Price: From Docs POV, strong preference for one canonical term. We can do:
- Heading: Tool calling
- First paragraph: “Tool calling (sometimes called function calling) lets you…”
- Add redirect anchors so searching “function calling” lands on the right section.

Wei Chen: Agree. The Hosted API docs currently say “function calling” in 2 pages. If we standardize on “tool calling,” I can update those and leave an explicit note for 1-2 releases.

Monica Patel: +1. SDK docs are currently mixed, and support keeps quoting “function calling” back at us. Canonical term will help.

Ibrahim Khan: Re streaming event names: yes, please keep “events” + the actual `type` values. We’ve seen users assume the event stream is just token text.

Ibrahim Khan: Also suggest we avoid “delta” as a noun in prose (folks interpret it as “diff”), but keep it in code and event type strings. E.g. “You’ll receive incremental updates (deltas)…”

Sabrina James: For structured output wording: can we be explicit that it’s schema-based and not “best-effort JSON”? That’s where the silent parse failure confusion comes from.

Henry Cho: Yes. Proposed phrasing: “Structured output returns model output that is validated against your JSON Schema; if validation fails, you can retry with stricter instructions.”

Nikhil Sharma: +1, but careful on guarantees. We should say “we validate” not “the model guarantees.” Also note what happens on failure (error + partial text?) so users don’t assume it always succeeds.

Elliot Price: Draft changelog line currently:
“Refreshed streaming/tool calling/structured output examples across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Clarified stream event semantics and added safer tool calling patterns.”

Elliot Price: Is “safer” OK or do we want something more concrete like “added allowlist + argument validation patterns”? Marketing-wise “safer” reads vague.

Henry Cho: Good call. Let’s be concrete.

Henry Cho: Updated changelog proposal:
- “Updated streaming examples to use the current stream event model (including tool-call argument deltas).”
- “Updated tool calling examples to include tool allowlists and argument validation (recommended for production).”
- “Added structured output examples with JSON Schema validation and a retry-on-parse-failure pattern.”
- “Added troubleshooting guidance for stream disconnects, partial tool arguments, and schema mismatch errors.”

Connor O'Brien: From release coordination: please keep changelog phrasing consistent across SDK patch notes + docs-site changelog. If we say “retry-on-parse-failure” in one place and “auto-retry” in another, we’ll get questions.

Connor O'Brien: Also: do NOT imply a breaking change. These are example/docs updates; gateway behavior has been clarified but not changed for most users.

Monica Patel: +1. Let’s explicitly say “No API breaking changes; examples updated to match current recommended patterns.”

Wei Chen: For “structured output” term: I’d like one FAQ bullet “Is this the same as JSON mode?” Answer: “Older docs used ‘JSON mode’ loosely; use ‘structured output’ with JSON Schema for stricter validation.”

Henry Cho: Works. I’ll add that.

Nikhil Sharma: Approval from Product on terminology + messaging as proposed, with the edits above:
- Tool calling primary, one parenthetical “aka function calling” early + glossary/FAQ.
- Structured output primary; explicitly mention JSON Schema; one FAQ mention re: “JSON mode.”
- Changelog bullets as concrete items + add “No breaking changes.”

Nikhil Sharma: :thumbsup:

Elliot Price: Great. I’ll mirror this phrasing in the docs PR description and the docs-site changelog entry.

Ibrahim Khan: I’ll ping Dana/Mateusz to make sure SDK READMEs use the same exact terms (tool calling / structured output) and that the streaming section references “stream events.”

Henry Cho: Thanks all. I’ll drop a final launch announcement draft in #devex for review, but Product sign-off is done on terminology.

Henry Cho: (Action item) Elliot/Wei: please ensure the docs pages include the “function calling” search hook for the next 30-60 days. Connor: I’ll reuse the “No breaking changes” line in release notes.

Connor O'Brien: ack. When you have the final text, send it to me for the release checklist so we don’t drift.
